2. Petitioner is the accused in Crime No.1812/2025 of Changanacherry Police Station, Kottayam,
registered alleging offences punishable under Sections 366, 376(1), 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short 'IPC') and Sections 3(a), 4(1), 5(l) and 6(1) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (for short 'POCSO Act').
3.

sentences.text: According to the prosecution, the accused became acquainted with the victim through Instagram during August 2023.
Thereafter the accused took her to his mother's residence on 10.08.2023 and raped her, after drugging her, in the bedroom of his residence.

Prosecution also alleges that in the last week of August 2023, the accused committed the offence again and also compelled her to perform oral sex after, threatening to publish her nude photographs and thereby committed the offences alleged.
4. Petitioner was arrested on 27.10.2025, and he has been in custody since then.

sentences.text: 5. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned counsel for the victim as well as the learned Public Prosecutor.
6. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that petitioner has been in custody since 27.10.2025, and hence he ought to be released on bail.
7. The learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application.
8. The learned counsel for the victim submitted that the victim apprehends that the petitioner may threaten her since they move in close circles with each other.
9. The victim is alleged to have been raped on her birthday in the residence of the petitioner.
In the same month, he is alleged to have compelled her to perform oral sex and also raped her once again.
However, it is noticed that even though the incident occurred in the month of August, 2023, the FIR was registered only on 22.08.2025 after a gap of two years.
The petitioner was only 19 years old at the time of the incident, while the victim was 17 years old.
The allegations are certainly serious.
However, it was submitted by the learned Public Prosecutor that investigation has been completed and final report has also been filed.
10. The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner is that the issue arose out of a romantic relationship and cannot be completely ignored.

However, that is an issue to be considered at the 2025:KER:92500 time of trial, especially since the allegation is that the victim was a minor and even a consensual relationship will fall within the offences under the POCSO Act.

11. Notwithstanding the above, taking into consideration the young age of the petitioner, the period of custody already undergone, apart from the fact that the investigation has been completed and the final report has also been filed, I am of the view that further detention would amount to punishment before conviction.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to be released on bail.

In the result, this application is allowed on the following conditions:-
(a) Petitioner shall be released on bail on him executing a bond for Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees fifty thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the court having jurisdiction.
(b) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required.
(c) Petitioner shall not intimidate or attempt to influence the witnesses; nor shall he tamper with the evidence or contact the victim or her family members.
(d) Petitioner shall not commit any similar offences while he is on bail.
